search_log: Independent Sol Medium audit on 2026-09-06, applying the user's requested reasoning setting in place of the methodology's historical Sol High instruction.

Searched the verified title and authors with “excerpt,” “first person,” “third person,” “point of view,” “alternating,” “Teacher,” and “Bennett”; opened the permissioned Bookreporter excerpt, official author page, OverDrive library sample record, Google Books results, Goodreads quote/review results, and the cited audiobook review.

Searched exact Teacher text including “THE TEACHER WALKED into Bryant Park,” “Teacher chucked his Treo,” and “The man in the beautifully tailored two-button Givenchy suit.” Results reproduced isolated quotations or an unauthorized full-text copy, not an authorized sustained Teacher passage; unauthorized full text was not used as evidence.

The OverDrive record offered an authorized sample, but its protected web reader did not expose searchable prose sufficient to locate a Teacher chapter. Google Books exposed metadata rather than usable interior prose. No credible explicit whole-book statement of grammatical person was located.

A Goodreads reader review describes switches between the Teacher's and detective's points of view and quotes short third-person Teacher prose, but it does not explicitly distinguish grammatical person and was not treated as sufficient whole-book structural evidence.
person_note: Independent Sol Medium review abstains. The permissioned opening and several sampled quotes securely establish sustained first-person Mike Bennett narration. However, q00362, q00366, and q00379 are isolated sentences with third-person subjects; under the methodology they are unmarked, not diagnostic proof of a nonparticipating narrator. The audiobook review establishes only separate performers, not different grammatical persons, and targeted research found neither an authorized sustained Teacher passage nor a credible explicit whole-book POV description. The book may alternate Bennett's first-person chapters with third-person Teacher chapters, but the available admissible evidence cannot distinguish that structure from a first-person book containing sentences about the Teacher, so ALTERNATING is not adequately supported.
